note: The single source of truth for what the site may claim. Every feature is shipped or soon; the page labels the soon ones. Change a status here and every page follows.

groups.name: Patterns
groups.line: Set the layout once. Lock what the brand decided.

groups.name: Swatches
groups.line: One brand kit, shared by every Pattern.

groups.name: Yarn
groups.line: Your photos, logos, video and copy, per project or shared by them all.

groups.name: Parts
groups.line: Small reusable pieces that drop into many Patterns.

groups.name: Motion
groups.line: Animation that is built frame by frame, so it eases like real motion.

groups.name: Voice
groups.line: Voiceover that is made on your own computer.

groups.name: Your model
groups.line: The same tools for you and for your model.

features.name: Locked and free stitches
features.summary: A locked stitch cannot be changed by whoever uses the Pattern, and that includes your model. The attempt is refused and reported.

features.name: The Pattern editor
features.summary: Draw, move and style stitches on a canvas, with the locked and free outlines always visible.

features.name: Fill mode
features.summary: Open a Pattern, change only the free stitches, and knit. Built for people who are not designers.

features.name: Batch knitting in the studio
features.summary: Knit many posts from one Pattern in one go, from a table you paste in. Your model can ask for variants too.

features.name: The Swatch editor
features.summary: Colours, fonts, logos and a written voice for one brand, in one place. Start one from the brand's website.

features.name: Yarn uploads
features.summary: Drop in photos, logos, video, sound, fonts and PDFs, sorted into folders. Every file lives in a folder you can open.

features.name: The Library
features.summary: Files every project shares, like a logo or a font you use for every brand. They are in each project's Yarn, beside its own, for you and your model.

features.name: Free stock
features.summary: Search free photos, video, music and sound from Openverse, with no key, and Pixabay, with a free key of your own. Add one to a project or the Library, and it keeps its credit and licence.

features.name: Parts
features.summary: A lower-third, a logo sting or a quote block, made once and dropped into many Patterns. Change one in the editor and every Pattern that uses it follows.

features.name: The frame-by-frame render engine
features.summary: A Pattern is a page with a timeline. The engine sets the time, takes a picture of each frame and lets ffmpeg do the encoding. The desktop app brings what it needs.

features.name: Motion in the editor
features.summary: Entrances, exits and loops on a timeline, scenes that change, and sound you can hear while you scrub, before you knit.

features.name: Local voiceover
features.summary: Turn a script into a voiceover with captions, in your computer's own voice or a speech server you run, with music under it.

features.name: An MCP server
features.summary: The tools the studio uses, from fill_slots to propose_swatch and knit_pattern, against the same store.

features.name: Your model inside the studio
features.summary: Bring your own key and ask for changes from the Ask page or beside the canvas, with a spending limit you set.

features.name: Posting to your accounts
features.summary: Post knits to Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, Threads, X and YouTube, now or at a time, through developer apps of your own. Your sign-ins stay on your computer.

features.name: Insights
features.summary: Each post's numbers from its platform, and what did better on your own accounts, said in plain sentences once there are posts enough to say it. LinkedIn gives no numbers to apps like this one.

features.name: A design system built as tokens
features.summary: Colour, type, spacing and the stitch outline are defined once and shared by the studio and this site.

features.name: Projects
features.summary: Several brands, each with its own Swatch, Yarn, Patterns, knits and posts.

features.name: Desktop installers
features.summary: An app for macOS, Windows and Linux that keeps itself up to date. Early builds are not signed, so each system warns once the first time it opens.
